title: Tutte's Flow Conjectures (Conjecture 1.2)
statement_text:
Let $G$ be an oriented 2-edge-connected graph.
1. $G$ has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
2. If $G$ does not have a Petersen graph minor, it has a nowhere-zero 4-flow.
3. If $G$ is 4-edge-connected, it has a nowhere-zero 3-flow.
context_text: Tutte initiated the study of nowhere-zero flows and observed their duality to colorings in planar graphs. He made three conjectures that have directed the field; despite a wealth of research, all three remain open.
paper_contribution: Cited as open background motivation. The paper does not directly advance these conjectures but instead proves exponentially many nowhere-zero flows exist under related edge-connectivity hypotheses, extending results of Seymour and Jaeger.
notes: Three sub-conjectures (5-flow, 4-flow, 3-flow) are grouped under a single labeled environment Conjecture 1.2 in the paper. References given as [13, 15, 3]; year not recoverable from the extracted text.
paper_title: Many flows in the group connectivity setting

title: Conjecture 1.10
statement_text: There exists a fixed constant $c > 1$ so that the following holds. For every 3-edge-connected oriented graph $G = (V, E)$ of order $n$, every abelian group $\Gamma$ with $|\Gamma| \geq 6$, and every $f : E \to \Gamma$, there exist at least $c^n$ flows $\phi : E \to \Gamma$ with $\phi(e) \neq f(e)$ for every $e \in E$.
context_text: Graphs may have loops and parallel edges. For an oriented graph $G=(V,E)$ and an additive abelian group $\Gamma$, a flow (or $\Gamma$-flow) is a function $\phi:E\to\Gamma$ such that at every vertex $v$ the sum of $\phi$ over the edges leaving $v$ equals the sum over the edges entering $v$; it is nowhere-zero if $0\notin\phi(E)$. Following Jaeger, Linial, Payan and Tarsi, $G$ is $\Gamma$-connected if for every $f:E\to\Gamma$ there is a flow $\phi$ with $\phi(e)\neq f(e)$ for every $e\in E$ (taking $f=0$ forces $\phi$ to be nowhere-zero); this is the flow analogue (dual) of group coloring, a choosability-type version of nowhere-zero flows. Jaeger et al. proved that every 3-edge-connected oriented graph is $\Gamma$-connected whenever $|\Gamma|\ge 6$; the conjecture asks for exponentially many such flows. The authors prove that, with $\ell=|E|-|V|$ and $|\Gamma|=k\ge 6$, the number of such flows is at least $\frac12(\frac{k-6}{2})^{\ell}$ for odd $k$ and $\frac12(\frac{k-4}{2})^{\ell}$ for even $k$; this is exponential for $k\ge 8$ but for $k=6,7$ gives only the existence of one flow, which they attribute to a shortcoming of their techniques. Hence the conjecture holds for all abelian groups except $\mathbb{Z}_6$ and $\mathbb{Z}_7$. For $\mathbb{Z}_7$ they have no interesting lower bound; for $\mathbb{Z}_6$ they prove a superpolynomial bound: if $\ell\ge 11$ there are at least $2^{\sqrt{\ell}/\log\ell}$ such flows (log base 2).
paper_title: Many flows in the group connectivity setting
